_about: Values the toolkit's tools read, kept out of the standards' prose (toolkit-standard §C clause F), grouped by the figma-standard section they serve. Naming is not here: the house's naming preferences are standards/naming-preferences.json, which every tool reads and the audit only checks against. audit-defaults: the house's answer for each setting; a project's audit-settings block overrides it section by section. Tools read one flat object per library, which tools/snapshot/projects.cjs auditContext builds by merging the sections and deriving the values under audit-keys.derived, so each fact is stated once. audit-keys: every key, what it means and the rule it serves. tools/toolkit-check/check-standards.mjs refuses a key that is unregistered or read by nothing, and heals a project value that restates a house default.

project.libraries: overrides for a components library the snapshot-routing block routes, keyed by its Figma file key; which libraries exist, and their roles, is the routing block's to say
project.language: the dialect of the words the toolkit writes for this project (en-US, en-GB); absent means en-GB, the toolkit's own, and by the maintainer's ruling it is never a house default (toolkit-standard §D 20)
project.interface: a project's own interface limits, over the house's (design-standard; read by tools/snapshot/projects.cjs interfaceLimits for ui-check, the parity engine and the docs site's structure check)

library.name: the library's display name
library.codeTarget: platform the component validator judges against
library.framework: component framework the code is built on
library.code: where the code lives: `repo` and `components` folder; how its markup names things where its framework profile does not (`partClass`, a regular expression whose group names an element's part; `iconClass`, one whose group names an icon); for a library built elsewhere, `parity`, the parity engine's facts about it (host and how to build it, its one tier, where its mappings are relative to the project's home, its generated token files), read by tools/parity/project.mjs loadParity
library.source: which is the components' source of truth: absent, Figma (the official contract is the snapshot's reading); "contract", the official contracts in the project's home (contracts/<component key>.json), which a snapshot never overwrites and Figma's reading is compared with. Set and cleared by tools/component-contract/official.mjs --switch
library.draw: how a contract is drawn into this library in Figma (tools/component-contract/to-figma.mjs): `iconContainer`, the name of the component an icon sits in; `scratch`, the key of the file a new component is drawn into, never the library (set in the contract editor's Settings)
library.frameworkComponents: Figma component name to framework component name
library._notes: free-text notes for people; no check reads them
library.icons: the icons section, for an icon library

icons.names: the icon set an icon library takes its names from (lucide); absent, names are not checked

optionOrder.<axis name>: the authored option order of that variant property (figma-standard rule 1; figma-standard rule 4; figma-standard rule 6)

variants.stateAxis: name of the interaction-state variant property (figma-standard rule 4)
variants.pointerStates: the state-axis options a browser or platform supplies (focus, hover, press), which code forces rather than takes as a prop (figma-standard rule 4)
variants.disabledAxis: the variant axis that sits immediately before the state axis (figma-standard rule 1)
variants.focusState: the state-axis option for keyboard focus, which every interactive component has (figma-standard rule 39)
variants.pseudoClasses: the CSS pseudo-class that draws each pointer state, keyed by its state-axis option: code takes these states from the browser, never as a prop (figma-standard rule 4; read by tools/component-contract/to-code.mjs for the stylesheet and to-markup.mjs for the parity mapping)
variants.firstAxis: the axis every component set leads with, where a project fixes one (project)
variants.sizeAxis: name of the size variant property (figma-standard rule 6)
variants.sizeAxisMatch: regular expression for property names that are size properties under another name (figma-standard rule 6)
variants.sizeShared: true to ask where one size name is drawn at different heights across components (figma-standard rule 6)
variants.emphasisAxes: the axes that sit between the size axis and the disabled axis, in order (figma-standard rule 1's Role → Feedback/…)

pages.statusMarker: leading page and component marker of work in progress, stripped from generated text (figma-standard rule 13)
pages.finishedMarker: leading page marker of a finished component page (figma-standard rule 11)
pages.categoryMarker: the mark a category header page starts with, before the category in capitals (figma-standard rule 11)
pages.deprecatedMarker: the mark a deprecated component's page and name carry (figma-standard rule 14)
pages.deprecatedCategory: category that holds deprecated pages (figma-standard rule 14)
pages.pinnedCategories: categories pinned last, in this order, before the deprecated one, which is always last (figma-standard rule 11; figma-standard rule 14)
pages.excludeCategories: categories left out of the audit (project)
pages.componentPages: regular expression for the pages an audit reads; absent, the pages carrying the finished or in-progress marker (figma-standard rule 11)
pages.familyCategories: categories whose members drop the family word, beyond those the data pairs by plural (`TABLES` holding `Table`); figma-standard rule 9, project
pages.dividerPage: regular expression for divider pages (figma-standard rule 11)
pages.pageMarker: regular expression for the leading marker stripped from page names when they are compared (figma-standard rule 11); compiled with the u flag where it allows, so \p{L} keeps a page name's accented first letter
pages.pageSections: the component page's section cards, in order (figma-standard rule 15)
pages.pageSectionComponent: the doc component whose instances are a page's section cards (figma-standard rule 15)
pages.matrixSection: the section present exactly when the page's primary component has variant axes or booleans (figma-standard rule 15)
pages.exemptPages: page names the detached-instance scan skips (figma-standard rule 27)

tokens.semantic: name of the semantic variable collection, or a list of names (project)
tokens.allowedKeys: variable collection keys a binding may come from (project)
tokens.brandGroup: path group in the source library whose child names the brand, `<brandGroup>/<brand>/...`; the extension check reads it (project)
tokens.textRole: the token path segment a text layer's fill binds to (figma-standard rule 28)
tokens.ratiosGrid: the documentation component a contrast matrix is drawn in, matched by name on the Foundations pages (figma-contrast-matrix)
tokens.local: variable collections the file keeps for itself (layout values one file needs), outside the system: no Foundations page, no findings (project)

components.descriptionPlaceholder: regular expression for a description that is a placeholder (figma-standard rule 25)
components.minDescription: fewest characters a real description has (figma-standard rule 25)
components.minTarget: smallest interactive target in px; 24 is WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8, level AA (figma-standard rule 26)
components.minText: smallest text size in px (figma-standard rule 26)
components.mechanismPadding: the smallest off-scale padding, in px, read as a mechanism (a progress or slider fill driven by padding) and raised as a question rather than a defect; absent, every off-scale padding is a defect (figma-standard rule 29)
components.overlayComponents: components whose instances cover the layer they sit in, such as a state layer: each is locked, stretched both ways, at 0,0 and its parent's size (a project's own rule, stated in its context document); absent, not checked

derived.componentPages: from finishedMarker and statusMarker, where a library sets none
derived.sectionHeader: from categoryMarker: the header page of a category
derived.pinnedLast: from categoryMarker, pinnedCategories and deprecatedCategory: the header pages kept last
derived.axisOrder: from sizeAxis, emphasisAxes, disabledAxis and stateAxis: the order a component's axes take (figma-standard rule 1), which a contract read from code and a drawing both follow

interface.maxSegments: the most choices a facet shows as segmented buttons; past it the facet is a menu (design-standard rule 4)
interface.shiftTolerance: CSS pixels a tab bar may move when its tabs are switched before the layout counts as jumping (design-standard rule 2)
interface.settleMs: milliseconds a page is given to settle after a tab is chosen before the layout is measured (design-standard rule 2)
interface.viewportWidth: the CSS width a page is measured at unless the run names one (design-standard)
interface.viewportHeight: the CSS height a page is measured at (design-standard)
interface.componentWindowHeight: the CSS height of the window a component is measured in, at viewportWidth, where the project's parity facts name no `window`: taller than a page's, so a tall component is measured whole (design-code-parity)
interface.phoneWidth: the CSS width a page's phone screenshot is taken at (frontend-build: look before you ship)
interface.shotMaxHeight: the tallest a full-page screenshot is taken, in CSS pixels, so a page of thousands of rows still produces an image (frontend-build: look before you ship)
interface.frameCell: the side, in CSS pixels of the page, of the cells a screen's picture and its frame's are compared in by mean colour: large enough to be blind to a half-pixel of hinting, small enough to be loud about a shape in the wrong place (design-code-parity, --shots)
interface.frameCellThreshold: the levels (0–255) a cell's mean colour may differ on any channel between a screen's picture and its frame's before the cell is drawn as differing (design-code-parity, --shots)

codeProps.inherited: the props every component takes from the platform (children, the global attributes), which no library's own types declare
codeProps.sameJob: the code props that do a design prop's job in the words code libraries share, keyed by the design prop's words: a join the rule cannot make by name. A framework's profile adds its own words after these
codeProps.notDesign: a regular expression for code props no design draws (handlers, styling escapes, test hooks), left out of the code's own API. A framework's profile adds its own

frameworks.instance: the class a component framework gives a component's root element, {Name} its own name for the component (tools/component-contract/from-code.mjs, where a library's `framework` names the profile)
frameworks.partClass: a regular expression whose group names the part an element is, from a class the framework gives it (tools/component-contract/from-code.mjs)
frameworks.partModifiers: a regular expression for the part names partClass catches that are a modifier, not a part (a size, a colour, a state)
frameworks.name: the framework's name as a reader knows it, for the pages and labels that name the other side of a comparison
frameworks.types: where the framework's own definition of a component is, relative to the code repo, `{Name}` its name for the component (the code audit reads each prop's values there)
frameworks.modules: the module path the framework's components are imported from, followed into the repo's node_modules when a type is read
frameworks.wrappers: the framework's type wrappers that take keys away like Omit and add members of their own
frameworks.unionWrapper: the framework's wrapper around a union of strings that a library may extend (its values are the union's)
frameworks.sameJob: the framework's own words for a design prop's job, added after codeProps.sameJob's
frameworks.notDesign: a regular expression for the framework's own props no design draws (slot plumbing, its styling escapes), added to codeProps.notDesign
